reason: E2 and E3 support grain refinement and TiC-induced hardness increases in laser cladding, but neither addresses TiN formation, the specific Ti-6Al-4V substrate, or the claimed wear reduction. E1 and E4 are irrelevant to the key premises. The quantitative improvement targets lack direct prior evidence.
premises: Laser cladding with high energy density and rapid cooling refines grains and increases hardness
In situ formed TiC in laser-clad coatings significantly improves microhardness via solid solution strengthening
Hard ceramic precipitates (TiN, TiC) inhibit dislocation movement and grain boundary sliding, enhancing hardness and wear resistance
A 50–60% hardness increase and 40–50% wear reduction are achievable with optimized TiN+TiC dispersion
